Light Browser 1.10.1

**Better: dragging a tab moves the tab**

Grabbing a tab used to reorder the strip without showing anything: the tab stayed where it was and positions jumped as you passed a neighbour. Now the tab follows your pointer, drawn above the others with a gap left where it came from, and the tabs it pushes past slide into their new places instead of snapping.

Pull it past the edge of the strip and the tab comes with you: a small floating copy — its title in the tab's own colours — follows the cursor anywhere on screen, including outside the window. Drop it there and it opens in its own window, exactly as before; come back to the strip and it slots straight back in.

Light Browser 1.10.0

**New: dark mode for websites**

Switch it on in the menu under **Theme → Dark mode for websites**, or on the Settings page. Sites that ship a dark theme of their own get it; everything else is darkened as it is drawn, so images and video keep their real colours. It applies to every open tab the moment you flip it — no reload, no restart — and follows your account if you sync.

**New: middle-click keeps you where you are**

Middle-click and Ctrl+click open the new tab behind the page you are reading instead of jumping to it. A normal link that opens in a new tab still comes to the front.

**Better: the saved-login list stays out of the way**

It no longer appears by itself on pages that are not a sign-in form, or on a page that shows a sign-out control — the clearest sign you are already signed in. Clicking a login field still opens it whenever you want it.

**Better: two-step sign-ins fill the right password**

On the second step, where the site shows the address you picked ("Welcome, you@example.com"), the password saved for that address is filled without asking again. If two saved logins share that address with different passwords, it asks instead of guessing.

**Better: updates install themselves quietly**

A new version is still checked hourly and downloaded in the background; it now goes in after three idle minutes, or a minute after you minimize, instead of waiting ten. It never interrupts playing media, a running download, a form you have typed into, or a private tab, and your tabs come straight back.

**Fixed**

- **Import could not see Opera.** Only `Opera Stable` was looked for, so an Opera GX install — its profile lives in `Opera GX Stable` — was invisible and none of its bookmarks or passwords came over. **Fix: Google sign-in.** "Couldn't sign you in – this browser or app may not be secure" no longer appears. Google's sign-in pages run an integrity check that refuses browsers whose built-in APIs were replaced; the fingerprint-protection hooks now stay off those pages and, everywhere else, report themselves as native code. Light Browser 1.6.0

**Download:** `LightBrowser-Setup.exe` (installer, per-user, no admin prompt). Portable: `LightBrowser.exe` + `filters/adblock.txt`.

`lbimport.exe` is the browser-import helper; the browser downloads and verifies it by itself when needed.
Verify: `*.sha256` sidecars.

## Privacy Engine 1.0 (Windows)
Incognito hides your history. Ghost hides your browser identity.

- **Seven levels**, each including the ones below: Normal, Private, Shadow, Mask, Ghost, Disposable, Ghost Internet. Set the level for new tabs on the Privacy page or open any tab in a level (menu, `Ctrl+Shift+N` for Private, `--private` / `--ghost` / `--mode=N` on the command line).
- **Private**: temporary cookies, storage, cache, service workers and permissions; no history, no saved logins; downloads leave the list with the tab.
- **Shadow**: every site runs in its own isolated environment.
- **Mask**: a standardised device instead of yours: canvas and audio (per-identity noise), WebGL, fonts, screen, CPU, memory, plugins, media devices, user agent, client hints; known fingerprinting hosts blocked; referrer removed cross-site.
- **Ghost / Disposable / Ghost Internet**: fresh temporary identity per tab (`GHOST #A71F`), UTC time zone, WebRTC relay-only; Disposable destroys its environment on close.
- **Personas**: named persistent identities (Work, Personal, Anonymous...) with their own cookies, storage, history and permissions, running in parallel.
- **Hide me**, **Erase trail**, **Destroy identity** on the Privacy page and in the menu.
- **Privacy dashboard** (shield button): per-site trackers/cookies/scripts blocked, fingerprint attempts, cleaned tracking URLs, third-party requests, referrers trimmed, device hints stripped, identity-exposure gauge, tracker relationship graph, network status.
- **Tracker protection on every level**: no third-party cookies to trackers (to nobody in private modes), no third-party ETag validators, tracking parameters removed from links, referrer trimmed to origin, crypto-mining scripts blocked, CNAME-cloaked trackers detected through DNS over HTTPS, EasyPrivacy + Fanboy's social + NoCoin lists added to the daily update.
- **Session-only permissions** in private modes: camera, microphone, location, notifications, clipboard... forgotten with the session.

## Also
- `--instance=name` runs an independent copy with its own profile (testing / second account).
- Everything from 1.5.x.

- **Search engine choice** (Google, Bing, DuckDuckGo, Brave, Yandex, Ecosia, custom) and **address-bar keywords**: `yt cats`, `w rust`, `gh light browser`, `!maps tbilisi`.
- **Tabs**: pin, color groups, right-click menu (unload, duplicate, close others), **vertical tab list** with 10+ tabs, hover tooltip with per-tab RAM, red badge on heavy tabs (click to free).
- **Lazy session restore**: your tabs come back as sleeping placeholders; only the one you look at loads.
- **Find in page** (`Ctrl+F`) with match count.
- **Download manager** (`Ctrl+J`): progress, pause/resume/cancel, open, show in folder, custom folder, ask-where-to-save.
- **Site permissions**: camera, microphone, location, notifications, clipboard and more are asked once per site and remembered.
- **Crash recovery**: dead pages show a reload button; a dead engine is rebuilt automatically.
- **Shared address-bar suggestions**: popular sites and pages from other users, grouped by kind (video, music, dev, news...).
- **EasyList element hiding** joins the daily filter update; YouTube in-stream ads are skipped, Spotify and Twitch ads muted.

## Faster and lighter
- RAM limit cascade: freeze, then unload background tabs one by one until the browser fits.
- Background tabs without playing media freeze 3 s after you leave them.
- Background-opened pages load images lazily and don't autoplay video.
- Preconnect on link/suggestion hover; 256 MB disk cache; back/forward cache.
- Filter lists fetched with conditional requests; visit reports batched.

body:
## What's new — Deep sleep

The closest a running browser gets to "fully on disk."

- **Deep sleep** — after the window has been minimized for about 3 minutes, Light Browser tears down its entire engine: every Chromium process (browser, GPU, renderers, utilities) exits. Only the small native shell stays, and its own memory is trimmed to disk, so the whole browser sits at a few MB of resident RAM while keeping your tabs. Restore the window and it rebuilds the engine and reloads the tab you were on.

Measured: one page active ~437 MB → deep sleep ~3 MB resident (engine gone, shell paged to disk) → restores in about a second.

- **Safe.** Deep sleep is skipped if any tab has unsaved text you typed or is playing audio.

This is the floor: below this you'd be closing the browser, not running it.

**Download:** `LightBrowser-Setup.exe`. Existing installs update themselves.

Website: **https://lightbrowser.net** · Made by [404 Friends](https://404friends.ge).

body:
## What's new — storage instead of memory

- **Working-set trim to disk** — when the window is minimized, when you're over the memory limit, or right after a background tab unloads, Light Browser now pushes its processes' cold memory pages out to the Windows pagefile (disk) with EmptyWorkingSet. The reported memory drops sharply; pages fault back in from disk when you use the browser again.

Measured: one page active ~437 MB; minimized drops to about 85 MB.

Honest note: this trades RAM for disk. It lowers resident memory but the pages live on the pagefile and come back on access (a tiny delay, negligible on an SSD). It's automatic and safe.

## What's new — the significant memory win

- **Background tab unloading** — a background tab left idle for about 10 minutes is now fully unloaded: its page process ends and its memory is returned to the system. Click the tab and it reloads instantly. Unloaded tabs show a ❄ snowflake and are dimmed.

  This is the biggest real memory saver. With many tabs open, only the ones you're using cost memory; the rest drop to near zero. It's the same approach as Chrome's Memory Saver and Opera GX's tab sleeping.

- **Safe by default.** A tab is never unloaded if it has unsaved text you typed, is playing audio or video, or was used recently. The tab you're looking at is never touched.

- **Away suspend** — when you leave the window unfocused for about 10 minutes, the active tab suspends too, freeing memory until you come back.

**Download:** `LightBrowser-Setup.exe`. Existing installs update themselves (SHA-256 verified).

## What's new

- **Cloudflare DNS over HTTPS** — Light Browser now resolves domains through Cloudflare (1.1.1.1) over an encrypted connection by default, independent of your system's DNS. This keeps sites reachable when the OS resolver is broken, slow, or blocking them, and hides your DNS lookups from the local network.

Note: a domain that does not exist in DNS (for example an expired site) still cannot load — no resolver can reach an unregistered name.
